thread.title: 15% Dividend Hike For Boeing Shareholders - The Boeing Company (NYSE:BA)

author: Dhierin Bechai
title: 15% Dividend Hike For Boeing Shareholders - The Boeing Company (NYSE:BA)
text:
Boeing ( BA ) share prices have been tanking quite a bit this year and they are 17.6% off their highs. Some investors have trimmed their position as Boeing’s dividend yield has been below 2% for the majority of the year. We can understand that investors trim part of the position to explore other dividend ideas. At the same time it should be noted that it is quite difficult for Boeing to increase its dividends fast enough because of the solid share price appreciation over the past few years driven by a combination of improving results and cash being deployed to buy back shares. So selling Boeing shares seems reasonable if you consider the yield, but if you look at the total return it makes a bit less sense. Nevertheless, we think that every investor should trim their positions as they see fit for their investment style.
Source: Boeing
In this report, which is part of a series that will focus a bit more on simple valuation methods, we will have a look at our expectations for Boeing’s dividend increase if any for 2019.
Dividend history Boeing has a strong dividend history as it has been paying dividends since 1942. However, it’s dividend growth streak is a lot shorter; Coming out of the financial crisis of 2008 and pressured by cost overruns on the Boeing 787 program, Boeing’s cash flow has been under significant pressure. Since 2012, Boeing has been increasing its dividend yield and since 2013 they have also been buying back shares as a second booster to shareholder value.
Dividend Table 1: Boeing quarterly dividend since growth (Source: AeroAnalysis, Data: Boeing)
The quarterly dividend gives a compounded annual growth rate of 22%. If the CAGR would be an indication of upcoming increase in Boeing’s dividend, then we could be seeing a $0.38 hike in dividends per share per quarter versus a hike of $0.29 last year. At the time of writing Boeing shares are trading at $323.22, so a $2.09 quarterly dividend would indicate forward annualized yield of 2.6%.
As can be seen, the dividend yield has been below 2% for the majority of 2018 primarily driven by solid share price appreciation. As share prices have been coming down recently, Boeing’s yield has ‘improved’ but not for the right reasons obviously. With a <2% yield, Boeing shares has been one of the lowest yielding stocks this year in the Dow Jones but still above popular brand names such as Apple ( AAPL ), Disney ( DIS ) and Nike ( NKE ). So the <2% yield is not as bad as it sounds. Surely there are better options at a <2% yield and a 0.6 point yield increase is not going to make Boeing a lot more attractive as a dividend pick.
Dividend trend Another method we used to estimate the dividend for 2019 is by simply putting a trendline over the dividends since 2011 and allowing a deviation. This would put the mid-point of the estimated dividend at $2.08, a 21.6% dividend hike with a high estimate of $2.24 for a 30.8% hike and a low estimate of $1.92 for a 12.3% hike. Based on this method, we are expecting that the actual increase will be around 12% to 22% resulting in a forward yield of 2.4 to 2.6 percent.
Total dividends The third and last method uses our combined expectations for dividends paid in 2019 and share repurchase. For 2019, AeroAnalysis expects Boeing to pay roughly $4.6B in dividends to shareholders and we hope to see Boeing buying back around 13 million shares, which would result in a $1.99 quarterly dividend or a 2.5% forward yield and a 16% increase in paid dividends.
Conclusion For 2019 we are hoping to see dividend growth of roughly 15%-22% percent compared to 20 percent last year and 30 percent the year prior to that. This would bring the quarterly dividend to $1.97-$2.08. In the table below, we have outlined how AeroAnalysis would view various dividend hikes,

What is important to keep in mind is that is not likely that we will see Boeing increasing dividend yield to the >3% levels seen in 2016 and there also is not a lot of reason to start spending a lot of cash on dividends. We think that the way things are looking now, there will be a lot of other companies that pay a better dividends than Boeing even after a new hike in dividends. While the focus lies on dividends for many investors, we deem the share repurchase program to be more valuable to investors to increase their total returns as the company is expected to continue growing its earnings in the future. Just because the dividend yield is not the most attractive, does not mean that Boeing is not a nice investment or that management does not return enough value to shareholders.
